name: 18-Crown-6
reason: Bulky macrocyclic ether (MW=264) tests GC MW>250 domain penalty boundary and viscosity saturation for high-ether-count molecules. Current benchmark lacks ethers above 7 O atoms.

name: Bis(2,2,2-trifluoroethyl) sulfone ethyl ether
reason: Fluorinated-sulfone-ether tri-hybrid molecule tests cross-term interaction of three co-occurring polar groups (ether+sulfone+fluorine). No existing benchmark entry combines all three.

name: Hexamethyldisiloxane
reason: Silicon-containing solvent — GC fragment-additivity has no Si fragments, so this tests the zero-fragment fallback and domain penalty behavior. Si-based electrolytes are an emerging class.

name: Trimethyl borate
reason: Boron-containing solvent additive. The GC model has boronate and borate fragments, but no B-containing benchmark entries exist to validate their contributions.

name: N,N-Dimethyltrifluoromethanesulfonamide
reason: Sulfonamide with CF3 — tests sulfonimide/sulfonamide fragment contributions. No sulfonamide compounds exist in the current benchmark, despite their relevance as Li-salt anions.

name: Tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether (Tetraglyme)
reason: Extended glyme chain (5 ether O atoms) tests Michaelis-Menten saturation behavior beyond triglyme (current longest glyme). Essential for validating ether saturation parameter.

name: 1,1,2,2-Tetrafluoroethyl-2,2,3,3-tetrafluoropropyl ether
reason: Highly fluorinated ether (8 F atoms) tests extreme fluorination domain penalty boundary (current F≥6 threshold) and viscosity saturation for perfluorinated chains.

name: Methyl cyanoacetate
reason: Nitrile-ester hybrid — tests cross-term interaction between nitrile and ester fragments. Current benchmark has nitrile-ether and carbonate-nitrile but no ester-nitrile combinations.

name: Tris(pentafluorophenyl)borane (BCF)
reason: Electron-deficient borane (MW=512) — extreme edge case testing MW>500 domain penalty, zero GC fragment matches (no fitting fragments for perfluoroaryl borane). Limits test for the GC fallback.

name: Methyl tributylammonium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide
reason: Ionic liquid pair — tests GC behavior for charged species. Current benchmark contains only neutral molecules, creating a blindspot for ionic liquid electrolyte formulations.
